---
name: slack-api
description: Slack Web API automation for sending messages, replying in threads, opening DMs, listing channels and reading history, searching, adding reactions, uploading files, and looking up users. Use when a user wants to post to Slack, DM coworkers, monitor or summarize channel conversations, notify a channel, react to messages, upload files to Slack, or perform any other Slack workspace action through the Slack API.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Drive Slack workspaces through the Slack Web API at `https://slack.com/api/`. Send and read messages, reply in threads, manage channels and direct messages, react to messages, upload files, and look up users and messages. For less common methods, read `references/api-reference.md` first for exact parameters, scopes, and examples.

## Authentication

1. Require a token. Check for `SLACK_TOKEN` in the environment first; otherwise ask the user for a token and use it only for this task:
   - Bot tokens start with `xoxb-` (an app installed into the workspace with the scopes the action needs).
   - User tokens start with `xoxp-` and act on the user's behalf.
2. Never guess, fabricate, or hard-code tokens. Never print a full token in output or logs.
3. Confirm the token before anything else:

```bash
curl -s https://slack.com/api/auth.test -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN"
```

Every call follows this shape: base URL `https://slack.com/api/<method>`, header `Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN`, JSON bodies with `Content-Type: application/json`. Responses are envelopes: `{"ok":true,...}` on success or `{"ok":false,"error":"<code>"}` on failure. HTTP 200 can still carry an API-level error, so always check `ok`.

## Resolve names to IDs first

Nearly every method takes IDs, not display names: channels `C...`, users `U...`, teams `T...`.

- Channel by name: call `conversations.list` with `types=public_channel,private_channel` and match on `name` (a channel named `general` has `name:"general"`, no `#`).
- DM partner: `users.lookupByEmail` (needs `users:read.email`) or `users.list` finds the `U...` id; then `conversations.open` with `users=U...` returns the DM `channel.id`.
- Current caller: `auth.test` returns `user_id` and, for bots, `bot_user_id`.

## Common tasks

### Send a message

`chat.postMessage` with a JSON body. `text` supports Slack mrkdwn; `blocks` builds rich messages:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel":"C1234567890","text":"Deploy finished :white_check_mark:"}'
```

### Reply in a thread

Add the parent message timestamp to the same call:

```json
{"channel":"C1234567890","thread_ts":"1710000000.123456","text":"Same thread"}
```

### DM a user

```bash
# 1. Resolve the DM channel id
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.open \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"users":"U1234567890"}'
# 2. chat.postMessage to the returned channel id
```

### Read history and threads

`conversations.history` (channel timeline) and `conversations.replies` (one thread) with `limit` and cursor pagination (see `references/api-reference.md`).

### React, update, delete

`reactions.add` (emoji name without colons, `timestamp` passed as a string), `chat.update`, `chat.delete`, all using the message `ts`.

### Upload a file

Two-step upload: `files.getUploadURLExternal` → POST the bytes to the returned `upload_url` → `files.completeUploadExternal`. See `references/api-reference.md`; the legacy `files.upload` shortcut is deprecated.

### Search and users

`search.messages` for workspace search; `users.info`, `users.list`, `users.lookupByEmail` for people.

## Incoming webhooks (no token needed)

If the user supplies a webhook URL like `https://hooks.slack.com/services/T.../B.../...`, send a notification with a single POST and no authorization header:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$WEBHOOK_URL" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"Hello from the CLI :wave:"}'
```

## Conventions and pitfalls

- Treat timestamps (`ts`, `thread_ts`, `timestamp`) as strings; they are floats like `1710000000.123456`.
- JSON quoting breaks easily. For long or complex payloads, write the JSON to a file with `write_file`, then post with `-d @payload.json`.
- Page through lists with `cursor`; stop when `response_metadata.next_cursor` is empty or absent.
- mrkdwn: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `>quote`, `<https://example.com|Label>`, `<@U123>` mentions. Set `link_names: true` to turn @names into mentions where supported.
- Prefer `blocks` over legacy `attachments` when building rich messages.
- On HTTP 429, honor the `Retry-After` header with backoff; never tight-loop retries. See the error table in `references/api-reference.md`: `not_in_channel` means invite or join the bot first, `missing_scope` means the app needs another scope.
- Keep outputs agent-friendly: truncate long channel or message listings (for example, first 20 items plus a count of the rest) and never dump raw paginated results.

## Resources

`references/api-reference.md`: endpoint cheat sheet with scopes, parameters, examples, error table, pagination, and rate-limit guidance. Load it whenever a method, scope, or error is unfamiliar.

# Slack API Reference

Companion to `SKILL.md`. Covers the Slack Web API (https://slack.com/api/) used for workspace automation.

## Contents

1. Request envelope and auth
2. Messages
3. Threads
4. Conversations and channels
5. History and search
6. Reactions
7. Files
8. Users
9. Scopes quick map
10. Pagination
11. Rate limits
12. Common errors

## Request envelope and auth

- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api/<method>`. Method names use dots, for example `chat.postMessage`.
- Headers: `Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN`; `Content-Type: application/json` when sending a JSON `-d` body.
- Every response: HTTP 200 with `{"ok":true,...}` on success, or `{"ok":false,"error":"<code>","needed":"<scope>","provided":"<scope>"}` on failure. HTTP 429 means rate limited (see below). Only retry transient failures; never retry `ok:false` logic errors verbatim.
- Tokens: `xoxb-` (bot) or `xoxp-` (user). An app must be installed in the workspace with the scopes each method needs; `missing_scope` names the required scope in `needed`.

## Messages

| Method | What it does | Key params | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chat.postMessage` | Send a message | `channel`, `text` and/or `blocks`, `thread_ts` | `chat:write` (add `chat:write.public` to post to public channels the bot has not joined; `chat:write.customize` for `username`/`icon_*`) |
| `chat.postEphemeral` | Send a message only one user sees | `channel`, `user`, `text`/`blocks` | `chat:write` |
| `chat.update` | Edit an existing message | `channel`, `ts`, `text`/`blocks` | `chat:write` |
| `chat.delete` | Delete a message | `channel`, `ts` | `chat:write` |
| `chat.scheduleMessage` | Schedule a message | `channel`, `text`, `post_at` (unix seconds) | `chat:write` |
| `chat.scheduledMessages.list` | List scheduled messages | `channel` (optional), cursor paging | `chat:write` |
| `chat.deleteScheduledMessage` | Cancel a scheduled message | `channel`, `scheduled_message_id` | `chat:write` |

Notes:

- `text` may be plain text or mrkdwn and is limited to 40,000 characters; supply `blocks` instead for rich layouts (`type:"section"` with `text.type:"mrkdwn"`, or `type:"divider"`, `type:"actions"`, ...).
- A successful send returns `channel` and `ts`; use that `ts` for thread replies, updates, deletes, and reactions.
- `chat.update` only works on messages the app itself posted.
- Ephemeral messages cannot be updated or deleted; scheduled messages need the returned `scheduled_message_id`.

Example with blocks:

```json
{
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "blocks": [
    {"type": "section", "text": {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Build failed* on <#C1234567890>"}},
    {"type": "divider"}
  ]
}
```

## Threads

Threads are ordinary messages with a `thread_ts`. To reply inside a thread, pass the parent message `ts` as `thread_ts` in `chat.postMessage`. To read a thread, use `conversations.replies` (`channel`, `ts` = parent message ts; cursor paging). Thread replies share the parent's `thread_ts` and include `parent_user_id`.

## Conversations and channels

| Method | What it does | Key params | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `conversations.list` | List channels/DMs the app can see | `types` (comma list of `public_channel`, `private_channel`, `im`, `mpim`), `exclude_archived`, `limit`, `cursor` | matching read scope (`channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read`) |
| `conversations.history` | Read a channel timeline | `channel`, `limit`, `oldest`, `latest`, `inclusive`, `cursor` | `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, or `mpim:history` |
| `conversations.replies` | Read one thread | `channel`, `ts` | same history scopes |
| `conversations.open` | Open or resume a DM or group DM | `users` (comma-separated `U...`) | `im:write` (DM) or `mpim:write` (group DM) |
| `conversations.create` | Create a channel | `name` (no `#`), `is_private` | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.join` | Join a public channel | `channel` | `channels:join` |
| `conversations.invite` | Add users (needed for private channels) | `channel`, `users` | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.kick` / `leave` | Remove a user / leave | `channel` (+ `user` for kick) | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.archive` / `unarchive` | Archive or restore | `channel` | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.rename` | Rename | `channel`, `name` | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.setTopic` / `setPurpose` | Set topic/purpose | `channel`, `topic`/`purpose` | `channels:manage` |

Notes:

- Channels have `id` (`C...`), `name` (no `#`), `is_private`, `is_member`, `is_archived`, `num_members`, `topic`, `purpose`. `conversations.list` only returns channels the app can see; private channels require the bot to be a member or invited.
- The bot must be a member before most reads and before posting to private channels; `not_in_channel` means join (public) or get invited (private). Apps with `chat:write.public` can post to public channels without joining.
- Timestamps `oldest`/`latest` are unix float seconds, inclusive per the `inclusive` flag.

## History and search

- `conversations.history`: newest-first timeline; each message has `ts`, `user` (or `bot_id`/`subtype`), `text`, `blocks`, optional `thread_ts`, `reply_count`, `reactions`. `limit` defaults to 100; page with `cursor`.
- `search.messages`: full-text search. Required param `query` (e.g. `deploy failed in:general from:@alice after:2024-01-01`). Pagination is page-based, not cursor-based: `count` (default 20, max 100) and `page`; response has `messages.matches[]` (each with `channel.id`, `user`, `ts`, `text`, `permalink`) and a `paging` object. Scope `search:read`.

## Reactions

| Method | What it does | Key params | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reactions.add` | Add a reaction | `channel`, `name` (emoji without colons, e.g. `white_check_mark`), `timestamp` (message `ts`, as a string) | `reactions:write` |
| `reactions.remove` | Remove a reaction | same as add | `reactions:write` |
| `reactions.get` | Get reactions on a message | `channel`, `timestamp` | `reactions:read` |
| `reactions.list` | Reactions by a user | `user` (optional) | `reactions:read` |

## Files

Two-step upload (current flow; `files.upload` was deprecated in March 2025 and should not be used for new integrations):

```bash
# 1. Ask Slack where to upload
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/files.getUploadURLExternal \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"filename":"report.pdf","length":12345,"alt_text":"Monthly report"}'
# -> {"ok":true,"upload_url":"https://...","file_id":"F..."}

# 2. PUT/POST the file bytes to the returned upload_url (multipart field "file")
curl -s -X POST "$UPLOAD_URL" -F file=@report.pdf -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN"

# 3. Attach the uploaded file to channels/messages
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/files.completeUploadExternal \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"files":[{"id":"F123","title":"Monthly report"}],"channel_id":"C1234567890","initial_comment":"See attached"}'
```

Notes:

- `length` in step 1 is the byte size of the file; compute it before uploading.
- Step 2 targets the Slack-provided `upload_url` host, not `slack.com/api`.
- Other methods: `files.info` (`file` id), `files.list` (channel filter, cursor paging), `files.delete` (`file`). Sharing links publicly needs `files.sharedPublicURL`. Scope: `files:write` (upload), `files:read` (read).

## Users

| Method | What it does | Key params | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `users.list` | List workspace users | `limit`, `cursor` | `users:read` |
| `users.info` | One user's profile | `user` | `users:read` |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | Find user by email | `email` | `users:read.email` |
| `users.profile.get` | Profile fields | `user` | `users.profile:read` |
| `users.profile.set` | Update profile/status | `profile` JSON | `users.profile:write` |
| `users.getPresence` | Presence (active/away) | `user` | `users:read` |

Notes:

- Users have `id` (`U...`), `name` (legacy handle), `real_name`, `is_bot`, `deleted`, and `profile` (with `email` only when `users:read.email` is granted). DMs never go to a deleted or bot-disabled user (`is_inactive`).
- To mention a user in text: `<@U1234567890>`.

## Scopes quick map

- Send/edit/delete messages: `chat:write`; public channels without joining: `chat:write.public`; custom name/icon: `chat:write.customize`
- Read channels/history: `channels:read`, `channels:history`, `groups:read`, `groups:history`, `im:read`, `im:history`, `mpim:read`, `mpim:history`
- DMs: `im:write`, `mpim:write`; channel administration: `channels:manage`, `channels:join`
- Reactions: `reactions:read`, `reactions:write`
- Files: `files:read`, `files:write`
- People: `users:read`, `users:read.email`, `users.profile:read`, `users.profile:write`
- Search: `search:read`

## Pagination

- Most list/history methods are cursor-based: pass `cursor` from `response_metadata.next_cursor`; when `next_cursor` is empty or absent, the end is reached. `limit` controls page size (defaults around 100).
- Bound your loops (for example, stop after 20 pages or a requested cap) and report totals to the user instead of dumping every page.
- `search.*` methods instead use `page`/`count` with a `paging` object.

Example loop for history:

```javascript
// Node 18+ (global fetch); channel C123, token from SLACK_TOKEN
const token = process.env.SLACK_TOKEN;
let cursor = '';
const messages = [];
do {
  const url = new URL('https://slack.com/api/conversations.history');
  url.searchParams.set('channel', 'C1234567890');
  url.searchParams.set('limit', '100');
  if (cursor) url.searchParams.set('cursor', cursor);
  const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
  const json = await res.json();
  if (!json.ok) throw new Error(`Slack API error: ${json.error}`);
  messages.push(...json.messages);
  cursor = json.response_metadata?.next_cursor ?? '';
} while (cursor);
console.log(`Retrieved ${messages.length} messages`);
```

## Rate limits

- Slack applies per-method rate tiers. HTTP 429 responses include a `Retry-After` header (seconds); wait that long, then retry once with backoff (doubling up to about 60 seconds).
- Practical ceilings: space out `chat.postMessage` to roughly one per second per channel, sleep briefly between history pages, and slow down file uploads. Do not parallel-burst the same method.
- HTTP 5xx and `internal_error` are transient; retry with backoff. `ok:false` business errors (`not_in_channel`, `missing_scope`, ...) should be fixed, not retried.

## Common errors

| error | Meaning and fix |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_auth` / `invalid_token` | Token missing, revoked, or malformed; recheck `SLACK_TOKEN` and run `auth.test`. |
| `not_authed` | No/invalid `Authorization` header. |
| `account_inactive` | The token owner's account is disabled. |
| `missing_scope` | App lacks the scope; the `needed` field names it. Ask the user to add the scope and reinstall the app. |
| `channel_not_found` | Bad id, or the app cannot see that channel (private/DM). Verify the id and scopes. |
| `not_in_channel` | App is not a member; `conversations.join` (public) or an invite (private), or use `chat:write.public`. |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived; unarchive it or pick another channel. |
| `invalid_blocks` / `invalid_arguments` | Payload schema problem; validate the JSON against Slack's block kit schema. |
| `no_text` / `msg_too_long` | Text missing or over the 40,000-character limit. |
| `already_reacted` / `no_reaction` | Reaction already present / absent. |
| `user_not_found` / `users_not_found` | Bad `U...` id; resolve via `users.lookupByEmail` or `users.list`. |
| `is_inactive` | Target user is deactivated; cannot DM them. |
| `file_not_found` / `bad_file` | Bad file id or the upload step did not complete. |
| `rate_limited` | HTTP 429; wait for `Retry-After`. |
| `restricted_action` | Workspace policy or approval required for this action. |
| `internal_error` | Transient Slack-side failure; retry with backoff. |

name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API to send and update messages, read channel history, manage conversations and users, upload files, search messages, and handle pagination, rate limits, and API errors. Use when Gemini CLI needs to query or act on a Slack workspace over HTTPS via curl, scripts, or bots.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Enables programmatic interaction with a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API (`https://slack.com/api/`). Cover messaging, channel and user discovery, file uploads, search, reactions, and the API conventions (auth, pagination, rate limiting, error handling) needed to make reliable calls.

## Authentication and Setup

- Every request must include a token. Prefer the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header; the deprecated `token` form parameter also works.
- Use environment variables so tokens never appear in code or prompts: `export SLACK_BOT_TOKEN="xoxb-..."` or `export SLACK_USER_TOKEN="xoxp-..."`.
- **Bot tokens** (`xoxb-`) act as the bot and only reach scopes granted to the app/bot.
- **User tokens** (`xoxp-`) act as a user. Apps for installed workspaces commonly use bot tokens.
- Token scope determines permission. Check per-method scopes in the Slack API docs (e.g., `chat:write` for `chat.postMessage`, `channels:history` for `conversations.history`). If a call fails with `missing_scope`, the token lacks the required scope.
- Some methods accept an `X-Slack-User` header to act on behalf of a user; only use when explicitly appropriate.

## Making API Calls

Base URL for every method:

```
https://slack.com/api/<method>
```

- GET requests take query parameters; POST requests take URL-encoded or JSON bodies. Slack recommends POST for methods that write data.
- Slack API responses are always JSON: `{"ok": true, ...}` on success, `{"ok": false, "error": "<error_code>"}` on failure.
- Always check `ok` before using the result; never assume success from HTTP 200 alone (Slack returns HTTP 200 even for many API errors).
- Example (send a message):

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel": "C1234567890", "text": "Hello from Gemini CLI"}'
```

- Example (list conversations, GET):

```bash
curl -s "https://slack.com/api/conversations.list?limit=100" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN"
```

## Common Operations

### Messaging

- **Send a message**: `chat.postMessage` with `channel` (ID preferred; names like `#general` only work for public channels and may be deprecated for some token types), `text`, optional `blocks`, `attachments`, `thread_ts`, `mrkdwn` (default true; set false to send literal text).
- **Message blocks** (`blocks`) are the modern rich-content format. Keep `text` as a plain-text fallback/notification summary even when using blocks.
- **Reply in a thread**: pass `thread_ts` set to the parent message's `ts`.
- **Update a message**: `chat.update` with `channel`, `ts`, and new `text`/`blocks`.
- **Delete a message**: `chat.delete` with `channel` and `ts`.
- **Add emoji reaction**: `reactions.add` with `channel`, `name` (no colons), and `timestamp`.
- **Ephemeral messages**: `chat.postEphemeral` sends a message only one user sees (needs `user` field).
- **Schedule**: `chat.scheduleMessage` with `post_at` (Unix timestamp; max 120 days ahead).

### Conversations and History

- **Find a channel ID**: `conversations.list` with `types` (`public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim`), `limit` (1–999), and `cursor` pagination. Filter client-side by `name` or `id`.
- **Get channel info**: `conversations.info` with `channel`.
- **Channel history**: `conversations.history` with `channel`; returns newest-first messages up to `limit` (max 999); supports `oldest`/`latest` Unix timestamps and `inclusive`. Join a channel first (`conversations.join`) if the bot is not a member and the channel is public.
- **Open an IM**: `conversations.open` with `users` (comma-separated IDs) returns the `im` channel ID for direct messaging.
- **List channel members**: `conversations.members` with `channel` (paginated).
- Timestamps (`ts`) are strings like `"1620000000.123400"`; treat them as strings, never floats, to avoid precision loss. `ts` doubles as the message ID for updates, deletes, and replies.

### Users

- **List users**: `users.list` (paginated) or `users.conversations` to list conversations. Filter by `is_bot`, `deleted`, or `name`.
- **Get one user**: `users.info` with `user`. Look up users by exact match of `name` or by email via `users.lookupByEmail` with `email`.
- **Set presence**: `users.setPresence` with `presence` (`auto` or `away`) when the token permits.
- User IDs look like `U1234567890`; use `conversations.open` + `users.info` to resolve a display name to an ID.

### Files and Search

- **Upload a file**: `files.upload` (multipart/form-data) with `channels`, `file`, `filename`, `initial_comment`, `title`. Newer Slack apps should prefer `files.getUploadURLExternal` + `files.completeUploadExternal` for uploads > 20 MB, then optionally `files.sharedPublicURL`.
- **Search messages**: `search.messages` with `query` (supports Slack search syntax like `in:#channel from:@user after:2024-01-01`), `count`, `sort` (`score` or `timestamp`), `sort_dir`. Needs the `search:read` scope.
- **Get a file**: `files.info`; download through the `url_private` with the token as a Bearer header.

## Pagination

Most list endpoints return `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Loop while it is non-empty:

```bash
cursor=""
while :; do
  resp=$(curl -s "https://slack.com/api/conversations.list?limit=200&cursor=$cursor" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN")
  # process $resp, then:
  cursor=$(echo "$resp" | jq -r '.response_metadata.next_cursor // empty')
  [ -z "$cursor" ] && break
done
```

- `limit` defaults vary (often 100) and max out at 999 for history, 200 for conversations.
- Do not filter by iterating when a parameter exists (`types`, `oldest`, `latest`, `query`).

## Rate Limits and Errors

- Slack applies per-method tier limits (tiers 1–4). `conversations.history`, `users.list`, and `search.messages` are heavily rate limited; cache results where possible.
- On `429 Too Many Requests`, read the `Retry-After` header (seconds) and back off; also honor the response body's `retry_after` field. Implement exponential backoff with jitter for transient failures.
- Common errors and fixes:
  - `not_authed` / `invalid_auth` — missing or bad token.
  - `missing_scope` — grant the scope in the app manifest and reinstall.
  - `channel_not_found` — use the channel ID, or invite/join the bot first.
  - `is_archived` — the channel is archived.
  - `not_in_channel` — bot must join (`conversations.join` or invite) before reading history or posting.
  - `ratelimited` — retry after the indicated delay.
  - `too_many_requests` — slow down; batch and deduplicate calls.
  - `invalid_blocks` / `invalid_blocks_format` — malformed Block Kit payload; validate block JSON.
- Retry idempotent reads on network failure; for writes, retry only after confirming the message was not already sent (e.g., no error and no duplicate from your own previous attempt).

## Workflow Guidance

1. **Resolve identifiers first.** Map human inputs ("post to #announcements and tell @alice") to channel and user IDs before acting: `conversations.list`/`conversations.open` and `users.list`/`users.lookupByEmail`.
2. **Fetch then format.** When summarizing activity, pull `conversations.history`, extract message `text` and `blocks`, then produce the summary; do not attempt to reconstruct message content from memory.
3. **Confirm before destructive or visible actions.** Sending to busy channels, deleting messages, or bulk actions should be confirmed with the user first. Prefer a dry-run listing of channels/users and messages to be affected.
4. **Choose the right integration surface.**
   - One-off queries/reports → direct Web API calls as above.
   - Ongoing event-driven automation → Slack Events API plus URL-verified request signing (validate `X-Slack-Signature` using the signing secret, reject replays with the timestamp rule).
   - Simple inbound notifications → incoming webhooks (`https://hooks.slack.com/services/...`) with JSON `{"text": "..."}`.
5. **Prefer timestamps to indices.** Always anchor updates/deletes/replies with the exact `ts` string of the target message.
6. **Mind context.** Truncate long histories and user lists before summarizing; large Slack payloads can overflow context. Pull only needed fields and page through results.

## Example: Post a Threaded Summary

```bash
CHANNEL="C1234567890"           # resolved via conversations.list
PARENT_TS="1620000000.123400"   # message ts to reply under

curl -s -X POST "https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"channel\": \"$CHANNEL\", \"thread_ts\": \"$PARENT_TS\", \"text\": \"Daily summary\", \"blocks\": [{\"type\": \"section\", \"text\": {\"type\": \"mrkdwn\", \"text\": \"*Daily summary*\\n3 new messages in #general\"}}]}"
```

## Resources

This skill currently ships only `SKILL.md`; keep operational details (organization-specific channel IDs, token conventions, or policy) in a `references/` file next to this one and link to it here when added. Any helper scripts for repeatable Slack operations belong in `scripts/` and should print clean, truncated, LLM-friendly output.

arguments.content:
---
name: slack-api
description: Slack Web API automation for sending messages, replying in threads, opening DMs, listing channels and reading history, searching, adding reactions, uploading files, and looking up users. Use when a user wants to post to Slack, DM coworkers, monitor or summarize channel conversations, notify a channel, react to messages, upload files to Slack, or perform any other Slack workspace action through the Slack API.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Drive Slack workspaces through the Slack Web API at `https://slack.com/api/`. Send and read messages, reply in threads, manage channels and direct messages, react to messages, upload files, and look up users and messages. For less common methods, read `references/api-reference.md` first for exact parameters, scopes, and examples.

## Authentication

1. Require a token. Check for `SLACK_TOKEN` in the environment first; otherwise ask the user for a token and use it only for this task:
   - Bot tokens start with `xoxb-` (an app installed into the workspace with the scopes the action needs).
   - User tokens start with `xoxp-` and act on the user's behalf.
2. Never guess, fabricate, or hard-code tokens. Never print a full token in output or logs.
3. Confirm the token before anything else:

```bash
curl -s https://slack.com/api/auth.test -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN"
```

Every call follows this shape: base URL `https://slack.com/api/<method>`, header `Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN`, JSON bodies with `Content-Type: application/json`. Responses are envelopes: `{"ok":true,...}` on success or `{"ok":false,"error":"<code>"}` on failure. HTTP 200 can still carry an API-level error, so always check `ok`.

## Resolve names to IDs first

Nearly every method takes IDs, not display names: channels `C...`, users `U...`, teams `T...`.

- Channel by name: call `conversations.list` with `types=public_channel,private_channel` and match on `name` (a channel named `general` has `name:"general"`, no `#`).
- DM partner: `users.lookupByEmail` (needs `users:read.email`) or `users.list` finds the `U...` id; then `conversations.open` with `users=U...` returns the DM `channel.id`.
- Current caller: `auth.test` returns `user_id` and, for bots, `bot_user_id`.

## Common tasks

### Send a message

`chat.postMessage` with a JSON body. `text` supports Slack mrkdwn; `blocks` builds rich messages:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel":"C1234567890","text":"Deploy finished :white_check_mark:"}'
```

### Reply in a thread

Add the parent message timestamp to the same call:

```json
{"channel":"C1234567890","thread_ts":"1710000000.123456","text":"Same thread"}
```

### DM a user

```bash
# 1. Resolve the DM channel id
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.open \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"users":"U1234567890"}'
# 2. chat.postMessage to the returned channel id
```

### Read history and threads

`conversations.history` (channel timeline) and `conversations.replies` (one thread) with `limit` and cursor pagination (see `references/api-reference.md`).

### React, update, delete

`reactions.add` (emoji name without colons, `timestamp` passed as a string), `chat.update`, `chat.delete`, all using the message `ts`.

### Upload a file

Two-step upload: `files.getUploadURLExternal` → POST the bytes to the returned `upload_url` → `files.completeUploadExternal`. See `references/api-reference.md`; the legacy `files.upload` shortcut is deprecated.

### Search and users

`search.messages` for workspace search; `users.info`, `users.list`, `users.lookupByEmail` for people.

## Incoming webhooks (no token needed)

If the user supplies a webhook URL like `https://hooks.slack.com/services/T.../B.../...`, send a notification with a single POST and no authorization header:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$WEBHOOK_URL" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"Hello from the CLI :wave:"}'
```

## Conventions and pitfalls

- Treat timestamps (`ts`, `thread_ts`, `timestamp`) as strings; they are floats like `1710000000.123456`.
- JSON quoting breaks easily. For long or complex payloads, write the JSON to a file with `write_file`, then post with `-d @payload.json`.
- Page through lists with `cursor`; stop when `response_metadata.next_cursor` is empty or absent.
- mrkdwn: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `>quote`, `<https://example.com|Label>`, `<@U123>` mentions. Set `link_names: true` to turn @names into mentions where supported.
- Prefer `blocks` over legacy `attachments` when building rich messages.
- On HTTP 429, honor the `Retry-After` header with backoff; never tight-loop retries. See the error table in `references/api-reference.md`: `not_in_channel` means invite or join the bot first, `missing_scope` means the app needs another scope.
- Keep outputs agent-friendly: truncate long channel or message listings (for example, first 20 items plus a count of the rest) and never dump raw paginated results.

## Resources

`references/api-reference.md`: endpoint cheat sheet with scopes, parameters, examples, error table, pagination, and rate-limit guidance. Load it whenever a method, scope, or error is unfamiliar.

# Slack API Reference

Companion to `SKILL.md`. Covers the Slack Web API (https://slack.com/api/) used for workspace automation.

## Contents

1. Request envelope and auth
2. Messages
3. Threads
4. Conversations and channels
5. History and search
6. Reactions
7. Files
8. Users
9. Scopes quick map
10. Pagination
11. Rate limits
12. Common errors

## Request envelope and auth

- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api/<method>`. Method names use dots, for example `chat.postMessage`.
- Headers: `Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN`; `Content-Type: application/json` when sending a JSON `-d` body.
- Every response: HTTP 200 with `{"ok":true,...}` on success, or `{"ok":false,"error":"<code>","needed":"<scope>","provided":"<scope>"}` on failure. HTTP 429 means rate limited (see below). Only retry transient failures; never retry `ok:false` logic errors verbatim.
- Tokens: `xoxb-` (bot) or `xoxp-` (user). An app must be installed in the workspace with the scopes each method needs; `missing_scope` names the required scope in `needed`.

## Messages

| Method | What it does | Key params | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chat.postMessage` | Send a message | `channel`, `text` and/or `blocks`, `thread_ts` | `chat:write` (add `chat:write.public` to post to public channels the bot has not joined; `chat:write.customize` for `username`/`icon_*`) |
| `chat.postEphemeral` | Send a message only one user sees | `channel`, `user`, `text`/`blocks` | `chat:write` |
| `chat.update` | Edit an existing message | `channel`, `ts`, `text`/`blocks` | `chat:write` |
| `chat.delete` | Delete a message | `channel`, `ts` | `chat:write` |
| `chat.scheduleMessage` | Schedule a message | `channel`, `text`, `post_at` (unix seconds) | `chat:write` |
| `chat.scheduledMessages.list` | List scheduled messages | `channel` (optional), cursor paging | `chat:write` |
| `chat.deleteScheduledMessage` | Cancel a scheduled message | `channel`, `scheduled_message_id` | `chat:write` |

Notes:

- `text` may be plain text or mrkdwn and is limited to 40,000 characters; supply `blocks` instead for rich layouts (`type:"section"` with `text.type:"mrkdwn"`, or `type:"divider"`, `type:"actions"`, ...).
- A successful send returns `channel` and `ts`; use that `ts` for thread replies, updates, deletes, and reactions.
- `chat.update` only works on messages the app itself posted.
- Ephemeral messages cannot be updated or deleted; scheduled messages need the returned `scheduled_message_id`.

Example with blocks:

```json
{
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "blocks": [
    {"type": "section", "text": {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Build failed* on <#C1234567890>"}},
    {"type": "divider"}
  ]
}
```

## Threads

Threads are ordinary messages with a `thread_ts`. To reply inside a thread, pass the parent message `ts` as `thread_ts` in `chat.postMessage`. To read a thread, use `conversations.replies` (`channel`, `ts` = parent message ts; cursor paging). Thread replies share the parent's `thread_ts` and include `parent_user_id`.

## Conversations and channels

| Method | What it does | Key params | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `conversations.list` | List channels/DMs the app can see | `types` (comma list of `public_channel`, `private_channel`, `im`, `mpim`), `exclude_archived`, `limit`, `cursor` | matching read scope (`channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read`) |
| `conversations.history` | Read a channel timeline | `channel`, `limit`, `oldest`, `latest`, `inclusive`, `cursor` | `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, or `mpim:history` |
| `conversations.replies` | Read one thread | `channel`, `ts` | same history scopes |
| `conversations.open` | Open or resume a DM or group DM | `users` (comma-separated `U...`) | `im:write` (DM) or `mpim:write` (group DM) |
| `conversations.create` | Create a channel | `name` (no `#`), `is_private` | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.join` | Join a public channel | `channel` | `channels:join` |
| `conversations.invite` | Add users (needed for private channels) | `channel`, `users` | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.kick` / `leave` | Remove a user / leave | `channel` (+ `user` for kick) | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.archive` / `unarchive` | Archive or restore | `channel` | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.rename` | Rename | `channel`, `name` | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.setTopic` / `setPurpose` | Set topic/purpose | `channel`, `topic`/`purpose` | `channels:manage` |

Notes:

- Channels have `id` (`C...`), `name` (no `#`), `is_private`, `is_member`, `is_archived`, `num_members`, `topic`, `purpose`. `conversations.list` only returns channels the app can see; private channels require the bot to be a member or invited.
- The bot must be a member before most reads and before posting to private channels; `not_in_channel` means join (public) or get invited (private). Apps with `chat:write.public` can post to public channels without joining.
- Timestamps `oldest`/`latest` are unix float seconds, inclusive per the `inclusive` flag.

## History and search

- `conversations.history`: newest-first timeline; each message has `ts`, `user` (or `bot_id`/`subtype`), `text`, `blocks`, optional `thread_ts`, `reply_count`, `reactions`. `limit` defaults to 100; page with `cursor`.
- `search.messages`: full-text search. Required param `query` (e.g. `deploy failed in:general from:@alice after:2024-01-01`). Pagination is page-based, not cursor-based: `count` (default 20, max 100) and `page`; response has `messages.matches[]` (each with `channel.id`, `user`, `ts`, `text`, `permalink`) and a `paging` object. Scope `search:read`.

## Reactions

| Method | What it does | Key params | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reactions.add` | Add a reaction | `channel`, `name` (emoji without colons, e.g. `white_check_mark`), `timestamp` (message `ts`, as a string) | `reactions:write` |
| `reactions.remove` | Remove a reaction | same as add | `reactions:write` |
| `reactions.get` | Get reactions on a message | `channel`, `timestamp` | `reactions:read` |
| `reactions.list` | Reactions by a user | `user` (optional) | `reactions:read` |

## Files

Two-step upload (current flow; `files.upload` was deprecated in March 2025 and should not be used for new integrations):

```bash
# 1. Ask Slack where to upload
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/files.getUploadURLExternal \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"filename":"report.pdf","length":12345,"alt_text":"Monthly report"}'
# -> {"ok":true,"upload_url":"https://...","file_id":"F..."}

# 2. PUT/POST the file bytes to the returned upload_url (multipart field "file")
curl -s -X POST "$UPLOAD_URL" -F file=@report.pdf -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN"

# 3. Attach the uploaded file to channels/messages
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/files.completeUploadExternal \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"files":[{"id":"F123","title":"Monthly report"}],"channel_id":"C1234567890","initial_comment":"See attached"}'
```

Notes:

- `length` in step 1 is the byte size of the file; compute it before uploading.
- Step 2 targets the Slack-provided `upload_url` host, not `slack.com/api`.
- Other methods: `files.info` (`file` id), `files.list` (channel filter, cursor paging), `files.delete` (`file`). Sharing links publicly needs `files.sharedPublicURL`. Scope: `files:write` (upload), `files:read` (read).

## Users

| Method | What it does | Key params | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `users.list` | List workspace users | `limit`, `cursor` | `users:read` |
| `users.info` | One user's profile | `user` | `users:read` |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | Find user by email | `email` | `users:read.email` |
| `users.profile.get` | Profile fields | `user` | `users.profile:read` |
| `users.profile.set` | Update profile/status | `profile` JSON | `users.profile:write` |
| `users.getPresence` | Presence (active/away) | `user` | `users:read` |

Notes:

- Users have `id` (`U...`), `name` (legacy handle), `real_name`, `is_bot`, `deleted`, and `profile` (with `email` only when `users:read.email` is granted). DMs never go to a deleted or bot-disabled user (`is_inactive`).
- To mention a user in text: `<@U1234567890>`.

## Scopes quick map

- Send/edit/delete messages: `chat:write`; public channels without joining: `chat:write.public`; custom name/icon: `chat:write.customize`
- Read channels/history: `channels:read`, `channels:history`, `groups:read`, `groups:history`, `im:read`, `im:history`, `mpim:read`, `mpim:history`
- DMs: `im:write`, `mpim:write`; channel administration: `channels:manage`, `channels:join`
- Reactions: `reactions:read`, `reactions:write`
- Files: `files:read`, `files:write`
- People: `users:read`, `users:read.email`, `users.profile:read`, `users.profile:write`
- Search: `search:read`

## Pagination

- Most list/history methods are cursor-based: pass `cursor` from `response_metadata.next_cursor`; when `next_cursor` is empty or absent, the end is reached. `limit` controls page size (defaults around 100).
- Bound your loops (for example, stop after 20 pages or a requested cap) and report totals to the user instead of dumping every page.
- `search.*` methods instead use `page`/`count` with a `paging` object.

Example loop for history:

```javascript
// Node 18+ (global fetch); channel C123, token from SLACK_TOKEN
const token = process.env.SLACK_TOKEN;
let cursor = '';
const messages = [];
do {
  const url = new URL('https://slack.com/api/conversations.history');
  url.searchParams.set('channel', 'C1234567890');
  url.searchParams.set('limit', '100');
  if (cursor) url.searchParams.set('cursor', cursor);
  const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
  const json = await res.json();
  if (!json.ok) throw new Error(`Slack API error: ${json.error}`);
  messages.push(...json.messages);
  cursor = json.response_metadata?.next_cursor ?? '';
} while (cursor);
console.log(`Retrieved ${messages.length} messages`);
```

## Rate limits

- Slack applies per-method rate tiers. HTTP 429 responses include a `Retry-After` header (seconds); wait that long, then retry once with backoff (doubling up to about 60 seconds).
- Practical ceilings: space out `chat.postMessage` to roughly one per second per channel, sleep briefly between history pages, and slow down file uploads. Do not parallel-burst the same method.
- HTTP 5xx and `internal_error` are transient; retry with backoff. `ok:false` business errors (`not_in_channel`, `missing_scope`, ...) should be fixed, not retried.

## Common errors

| error | Meaning and fix |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_auth` / `invalid_token` | Token missing, revoked, or malformed; recheck `SLACK_TOKEN` and run `auth.test`. |
| `not_authed` | No/invalid `Authorization` header. |
| `account_inactive` | The token owner's account is disabled. |
| `missing_scope` | App lacks the scope; the `needed` field names it. Ask the user to add the scope and reinstall the app. |
| `channel_not_found` | Bad id, or the app cannot see that channel (private/DM). Verify the id and scopes. |
| `not_in_channel` | App is not a member; `conversations.join` (public) or an invite (private), or use `chat:write.public`. |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived; unarchive it or pick another channel. |
| `invalid_blocks` / `invalid_arguments` | Payload schema problem; validate the JSON against Slack's block kit schema. |
| `no_text` / `msg_too_long` | Text missing or over the 40,000-character limit. |
| `already_reacted` / `no_reaction` | Reaction already present / absent. |
| `user_not_found` / `users_not_found` | Bad `U...` id; resolve via `users.lookupByEmail` or `users.list`. |
| `is_inactive` | Target user is deactivated; cannot DM them. |
| `file_not_found` / `bad_file` | Bad file id or the upload step did not complete. |
| `rate_limited` | HTTP 429; wait for `Retry-After`. |
| `restricted_action` | Workspace policy or approval required for this action. |
| `internal_error` | Transient Slack-side failure; retry with backoff. |

---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API to send and update messages, read channel history, manage conversations and users, upload files, search messages, and handle pagination, rate limits, and API errors. Use when Gemini CLI needs to query or act on a Slack workspace over HTTPS via curl, scripts, or bots.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Enables programmatic interaction with a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API (`https://slack.com/api/`). Cover messaging, channel and user discovery, file uploads, search, reactions, and the API conventions (auth, pagination, rate limiting, error handling) needed to make reliable calls.

## Authentication and Setup

- Every request must include a token. Prefer the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header; the deprecated `token` form parameter also works.
- Use environment variables so tokens never appear in code or prompts: `export SLACK_BOT_TOKEN="xoxb-..."` or `export SLACK_USER_TOKEN="xoxp-..."`.
- **Bot tokens** (`xoxb-`) act as the bot and only reach scopes granted to the app/bot.
- **User tokens** (`xoxp-`) act as a user. Apps for installed workspaces commonly use bot tokens.
- Token scope determines permission. Check per-method scopes in the Slack API docs (e.g., `chat:write` for `chat.postMessage`, `channels:history` for `conversations.history`). If a call fails with `missing_scope`, the token lacks the required scope.
- Some methods accept an `X-Slack-User` header to act on behalf of a user; only use when explicitly appropriate.

## Making API Calls

Base URL for every method:

```
https://slack.com/api/<method>
```

- GET requests take query parameters; POST requests take URL-encoded or JSON bodies. Slack recommends POST for methods that write data.
- Slack API responses are always JSON: `{"ok": true, ...}` on success, `{"ok": false, "error": "<error_code>"}` on failure.
- Always check `ok` before using the result; never assume success from HTTP 200 alone (Slack returns HTTP 200 even for many API errors).
- Example (send a message):

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel": "C1234567890", "text": "Hello from Gemini CLI"}'
```

- Example (list conversations, GET):

```bash
curl -s "https://slack.com/api/conversations.list?limit=100" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN"
```

## Common Operations

### Messaging

- **Send a message**: `chat.postMessage` with `channel` (ID preferred; names like `#general` only work for public channels and may be deprecated for some token types), `text`, optional `blocks`, `attachments`, `thread_ts`, `mrkdwn` (default true; set false to send literal text).
- **Message blocks** (`blocks`) are the modern rich-content format. Keep `text` as a plain-text fallback/notification summary even when using blocks.
- **Reply in a thread**: pass `thread_ts` set to the parent message's `ts`.
- **Update a message**: `chat.update` with `channel`, `ts`, and new `text`/`blocks`.
- **Delete a message**: `chat.delete` with `channel` and `ts`.
- **Add emoji reaction**: `reactions.add` with `channel`, `name` (no colons), and `timestamp`.
- **Ephemeral messages**: `chat.postEphemeral` sends a message only one user sees (needs `user` field).
- **Schedule**: `chat.scheduleMessage` with `post_at` (Unix timestamp; max 120 days ahead).

### Conversations and History

- **Find a channel ID**: `conversations.list` with `types` (`public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim`), `limit` (1–999), and `cursor` pagination. Filter client-side by `name` or `id`.
- **Get channel info**: `conversations.info` with `channel`.
- **Channel history**: `conversations.history` with `channel`; returns newest-first messages up to `limit` (max 999); supports `oldest`/`latest` Unix timestamps and `inclusive`. Join a channel first (`conversations.join`) if the bot is not a member and the channel is public.
- **Open an IM**: `conversations.open` with `users` (comma-separated IDs) returns the `im` channel ID for direct messaging.
- **List channel members**: `conversations.members` with `channel` (paginated).
- Timestamps (`ts`) are strings like `"1620000000.123400"`; treat them as strings, never floats, to avoid precision loss. `ts` doubles as the message ID for updates, deletes, and replies.

### Users

- **List users**: `users.list` (paginated) or `users.conversations` to list conversations. Filter by `is_bot`, `deleted`, or `name`.
- **Get one user**: `users.info` with `user`. Look up users by exact match of `name` or by email via `users.lookupByEmail` with `email`.
- **Set presence**: `users.setPresence` with `presence` (`auto` or `away`) when the token permits.
- User IDs look like `U1234567890`; use `conversations.open` + `users.info` to resolve a display name to an ID.

### Files and Search

- **Upload a file**: `files.upload` (multipart/form-data) with `channels`, `file`, `filename`, `initial_comment`, `title`. Newer Slack apps should prefer `files.getUploadURLExternal` + `files.completeUploadExternal` for uploads > 20 MB, then optionally `files.sharedPublicURL`.
- **Search messages**: `search.messages` with `query` (supports Slack search syntax like `in:#channel from:@user after:2024-01-01`), `count`, `sort` (`score` or `timestamp`), `sort_dir`. Needs the `search:read` scope.
- **Get a file**: `files.info`; download through the `url_private` with the token as a Bearer header.

## Pagination

Most list endpoints return `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Loop while it is non-empty:

```bash
cursor=""
while :; do
  resp=$(curl -s "https://slack.com/api/conversations.list?limit=200&cursor=$cursor" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN")
  # process $resp, then:
  cursor=$(echo "$resp" | jq -r '.response_metadata.next_cursor // empty')
  [ -z "$cursor" ] && break
done
```

- `limit` defaults vary (often 100) and max out at 999 for history, 200 for conversations.
- Do not filter by iterating when a parameter exists (`types`, `oldest`, `latest`, `query`).

## Rate Limits and Errors

- Slack applies per-method tier limits (tiers 1–4). `conversations.history`, `users.list`, and `search.messages` are heavily rate limited; cache results where possible.
- On `429 Too Many Requests`, read the `Retry-After` header (seconds) and back off; also honor the response body's `retry_after` field. Implement exponential backoff with jitter for transient failures.
- Common errors and fixes:
  - `not_authed` / `invalid_auth` — missing or bad token.
  - `missing_scope` — grant the scope in the app manifest and reinstall.
  - `channel_not_found` — use the channel ID, or invite/join the bot first.
  - `is_archived` — the channel is archived.
  - `not_in_channel` — bot must join (`conversations.join` or invite) before reading history or posting.
  - `ratelimited` — retry after the indicated delay.
  - `too_many_requests` — slow down; batch and deduplicate calls.
  - `invalid_blocks` / `invalid_blocks_format` — malformed Block Kit payload; validate block JSON.
- Retry idempotent reads on network failure; for writes, retry only after confirming the message was not already sent (e.g., no error and no duplicate from your own previous attempt).

## Workflow Guidance

1. **Resolve identifiers first.** Map human inputs ("post to #announcements and tell @alice") to channel and user IDs before acting: `conversations.list`/`conversations.open` and `users.list`/`users.lookupByEmail`.
2. **Fetch then format.** When summarizing activity, pull `conversations.history`, extract message `text` and `blocks`, then produce the summary; do not attempt to reconstruct message content from memory.
3. **Confirm before destructive or visible actions.** Sending to busy channels, deleting messages, or bulk actions should be confirmed with the user first. Prefer a dry-run listing of channels/users and messages to be affected.
4. **Choose the right integration surface.**
   - One-off queries/reports → direct Web API calls as above.
   - Ongoing event-driven automation → Slack Events API plus URL-verified request signing (validate `X-Slack-Signature` using the signing secret, reject replays with the timestamp rule).
   - Simple inbound notifications → incoming webhooks (`https://hooks.slack.com/services/...`) with JSON `{"text": "..."}`.
5. **Prefer timestamps to indices.** Always anchor updates/deletes/replies with the exact `ts` string of the target message.
6. **Mind context.** Truncate long histories and user lists before summarizing; large Slack payloads can overflow context. Pull only needed fields and page through results.

## Example: Post a Threaded Summary

```bash
CHANNEL="C1234567890"           # resolved via conversations.list
PARENT_TS="1620000000.123400"   # message ts to reply under

curl -s -X POST "https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"channel\": \"$CHANNEL\", \"thread_ts\": \"$PARENT_TS\", \"text\": \"Daily summary\", \"blocks\": [{\"type\": \"section\", \"text\": {\"type\": \"mrkdwn\", \"text\": \"*Daily summary*\\n3 new messages in #general\"}}]}"
```
